---
title: "3 · Elements of Deep Learning: from MNIST to the 2D Ising Model"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

The anatomy of a neural network, loss functions for regression and classification, the zoo of architectures and training by gradient descent. Two "hello world" examples: MNIST digits, classified by a feed-forward network with the categorical cross-entropy, and CIFAR-10 images, where convolutional networks capture spatial correlations and L1/L2 regularisation, dropout and batch normalisation fight overfitting; optimisers from stochastic gradient descent to Adam. A physics example: the 2D Ising model, Onsager's solution, Monte Carlo samples from the Gibbs distribution, and the prediction confidence of a network that locates the critical temperature; the lecture closes with the Chinese Room thought experiment and the Hopfield network.
